summary: Moot on master and overlapped by the running triton-map-align-small-m-port. The 3.2 us bs=1 gap it was written to explain (80.2 vs 77.0 us) no longer exists: master's bs=1 is 55.3 vs SGLang 77.3 us, and the align-256 review already traced the gap to the small-batch align kernel. At bs<=32 the port replaces this align call entirely, drops remote routes itself, and its prepare() self-check logs SGLang's r_pad against the true n_pad, which answers this probe's question deterministically and costs no timing run.
justification: A: The mechanism is weak and the motivation is stale. (1) The premise is gone. The 80.2 vs 77.0 us bs=1 comparison is from before post-expert-norm-triton-small-m landed. In bacd1f502f4e46fa master runs bs=1 at 55.3 us against SGLang's 77.3, and bs=8 and bs=16 also beat SGLang clearly. Only bs=32 trails (206.9 vs 204.2). (2) The 3.2 us was already explained by a different mechanism. The align-256-experts-below-128 review found that at numel<1024 with 32 experts, sgl-kernel picks moe_align_block_size_small_batch_expert_kernel (4.4-6.5 us), while the 256-expert call and bs>=128 use the regular kernel (2.6-2.8 us). align-single-token-ep's 1.2 us kernel recovered that 3.2 us almost exactly, and its Marlin time rose rather than fell, which argues against a phantom m-block. (3) The cost is understated. align_map[topk_ids] is a second int32-indexed gather, which in master's profile is index_elementwise_kernel (1.7-3.3 us) plus, very likely, an unrolled_elementwise int64 index cast (1.4-3.2 us). That is ~3-6 us per shape, not 1-2. At bs=1, if the phantom block does not exist, the result is a ~5-10% loss on a 55 us shape. (4) Risk: if sgl-kernel's align has no >=num_experts guard, the sentinel 32 indexes past its 32 counters or produces block_experts=32 beyond the bank, which is a fault, not a measurement. Weakest link: the whole expected gain depends on an unverified phantom-block behaviour that the existing evidence (align-single-token-ep's Marlin time, the small-batch kernel explanation) already points against. The expected directions are consistent with TASK.md's equal weights, but they would be read on top of ~3-6 us of added launches at every shape.
confounders: sglang-marlin-path-parity: it defines the 32-expert moe_align_block_size call and the -1 expert_map that this probe modifies. The question is a sub-question of that patch's one deliberate difference from baseline.py, and align-256-experts-below-128 (neutral, 1.000x) already A/B'd that difference at M<128 without finding a Marlin-side effect.

post-expert-norm-triton-small-m: no timing confound, because it consumes local_ids, which stay unchanged. But it moved bs=1/8/16 far ahead of SGLang, so this probe's motivating gap is no longer present on master.
interference: Overlap with triton-map-align-small-m-port (running, job c2feb68aafb44aeb): direct, and it covers 4 of 6 shapes. For num_tokens<=32 the port deletes the moe_align_block_size call this hypothesis would modify and replaces it with a Triton counting sort in which remote routes get no bucket. That is exactly the end state this probe wants (remote routes dropped from sorted_ids), plus removal of the gather and cast launches. If the port lands, this change at bs<=32 is dead code. Whether or not it lands, its prepare() self-check prints n_pad vs SGLang r_pad per case (T in {1,8,16,32}, 5 routings, 3 local_starts), which settles whether the 32-expert small-batch kernel buckets -1 routes. It does so deterministically and for free, which a noisy Marlin timing cannot. The remaining slice, bs=128/256 on the regular align kernel, is expected flat by the hypothesis itself, and profiled Marlin time drifts 20-30% on identical code there, so a check spent on it would not be interpretable. No companion would rescue it: an ab-revert of parity is meaningless, there is nothing to tune, and the only sub-change (the extra gather) is pure cost. Re-queue only if the port's pad lines show r_pad > n_pad (SGLang buckets -1 routes). Even then, re-scope it to num_tokens>=128 only, use a non-gather sentinel construction, and add an untimed prepare() check that r_pad shrinks on the regular kernel before spending a check.
rules_flags: No rule break in principle: align_map is a prepare-time table built from config, not from inputs, and the per-call gather runs inside kernel_fn with no host sync.

Correctness/safety risk, not a rule: an id equal to num_experts passed to sgl-kernel's align may index out of bounds (counters, or block_experts=32 handed to Marlin with is_ep=True, which reads past the 32-expert bank). This would show up as a test failure or an illegal memory access on the GPU.
open_questions: From triton-map-align-small-m-port's log: do any self-check cases print r_pad > n_pad [DIFF]? If none do, the 32-expert small-batch align does not bucket -1 routes at T<=32, and this hypothesis's mechanism is refuted for bs<=32.

If DIFF lines appear, does the regular moe_align_block_size_kernel (numel>=1024, bs=128/256) bucket -1 routes as well? An untimed prepare() comparison of n_padded on synthetic ids with and without remote routes answers this without a check.
Does sgl-kernel's align bounds-check ids >= num_experts at all? That needs to be known before any sentinel variant is built.
